items.name: tokens
items.title: Semantic tokens
items.description: The color, type, space, shape and motion custom properties every block reads, with neutral defaults.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import src/styles/tokens.css once in your layout, then override the roles in your own theme. Blocks fall back to the same values, so this item is optional.

meta.useWhen: A project has no theme yet and you want one place to set colors, fonts, type scale, spacing and radius for every block.
meta.avoidWhen: The site already defines these roles, as every Site Boulder starter does. Keep the site's own tokens.

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: A link or button with solid, outline and quiet variants that read the accent, radius and action-weight tokens.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/ui/Button.astro. Pass href for a link; omit it for a button.

meta.useWhen: You need consistent primary and secondary actions across sections.
meta.avoidWhen: A plain text link reads better, such as inside running prose.

items.name: header-floating
items.title: Floating header
items.description: A detached, rounded navigation bar that floats below the top edge with a translucent surface and a native popover menu on narrow screens.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/HeaderFloating.astro. The narrow-screen menu uses the HTML popover attribute and needs no JavaScript.

meta.useWhen: The site has four to six destinations plus one primary action, and the page below has imagery or color the bar can float over.
meta.avoidWhen: The site is a quiet single page, or the brand needs a large masthead. Use header-minimal or header-editorial instead.

items.name: header-editorial
items.title: Editorial header
items.description: A magazine masthead: a centered wordmark with tagline, a top line for an issue or place, and section links between double rules that wrap instead of hiding.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: The site publishes writing or has distinct sections, and the name deserves to be the loudest thing at the top.
meta.avoidWhen: The site needs a primary action in the header more than a wordmark, or the name is long. Use header-floating or header-minimal.

items.name: header-transparent
items.title: Transparent header
items.description: A header that overlays the opening image in light or dark ink, with a native popover menu on narrow screens and, where supported, a solid surface that fades in while scrolling.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/HeaderTransparent.astro and put a full-bleed opening such as hero-immersive directly after it.

meta.useWhen: The page opens with a full-bleed photograph or artwork that should start at the very top.
meta.avoidWhen: The opening is text on a plain background, or the image is busy where the header sits. Use header-minimal or header-floating.

items.name: header-minimal
items.title: Minimal header
items.description: A single quiet row: name, two to five links and an optional action. Links wrap onto their own row on narrow screens instead of hiding in a menu.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: There are only a few destinations and every one should stay visible, especially on phones.
meta.avoidWhen: There are more than five links, or the header should overlay imagery.

items.name: hero-split
items.title: Split hero
items.description: Headline, lede and actions beside one framed image or artwork, stacking copy-first on narrow screens.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/HeroSplit.astro. Pass image, or use the media slot for a picture, video or SVG.

meta.useWhen: There is one strong, real image or artwork that shows the actual work, and a clear first action.
meta.avoidWhen: There is no genuine image. Use hero-typographic rather than a stock or decorative picture.

items.name: hero-immersive
items.title: Immersive hero
items.description: A full-bleed photograph or artwork with the headline, lede and actions set in white over a contrast-safe gradient scrim.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/HeroImmersive.astro. It breaks out of a centered column and clips the page's horizontal overflow.

meta.useWhen: There is a striking, high-quality photograph or artwork of the real place, product or experience.
meta.avoidWhen: The image is a stock photo, low resolution, or bright across the bottom third. Use hero-split, which frames the image beside the text.

items.name: hero-typographic
items.title: Typographic hero
items.description: A large statement headline with one accented phrase, an optional lede and actions, and a ruled row of short facts.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/HeroTypographic.astro. Set emphasis to a phrase that appears in title.

meta.useWhen: The positioning sentence is the strongest material, or there is no imagery yet.
meta.avoidWhen: The headline runs past about fourteen words, or a photo of the real work would say more.

items.name: steps-numbered
items.title: Numbered steps
items.description: An ordered list of two to five steps with large numerals, set side by side on wide screens or one per line for longer text.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: Visitors need to understand a real sequence, such as how booking, a project or a course of care unfolds.
meta.avoidWhen: The items have no inherent order. Numbering unordered features is decoration; use features-editorial instead.

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.description: A vertical timeline of dated entries on a rail, with an optional current entry and labels in their own column on wide screens.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: Dates or phases carry the meaning: a company history, a project schedule or an event programme.
meta.avoidWhen: There are fewer than three entries, or the dates add nothing. A paragraph is clearer.

items.name: alternating-rows
items.title: Alternating rows
items.description: Rows that pair an image, or a large typographic figure, with a short text, alternating sides on wide screens.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: Each point has its own real image or one striking number, and the points read in order.
meta.avoidWhen: The rows would all use similar stock images, or there are more than five rows.

items.name: features-bento
items.title: Bento features
items.description: An asymmetric grid of related features with one large tile, wide and tall tiles, accent and outline tones, and whole-tile links.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/FeaturesBento.astro. Give the most important item size large.

meta.useWhen: Four to seven related capabilities differ in importance, and one deserves the largest tile.
meta.avoidWhen: The items are unrelated, equal in weight, or exactly three. A bento grid of unrelated boxes reads as filler; use features-editorial.

items.name: features-editorial
items.title: Editorial features
items.description: A large heading and intro that stay in view beside a ruled list of offers, each with a title, a sentence or two and an optional label.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>

meta.useWhen: Services or offers need a sentence each, and reading them in order matters more than visual variety.
meta.avoidWhen: There are only one or two items, or each needs an image. Use alternating-rows.

items.name: footer-minimal
items.title: Minimal footer
items.description: One quiet line: copyright, a short note such as an address or hours, a few links and an optional credit.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/FooterMinimal.astro. In a Site Boulder site, render it from SiteFooter.astro and pass the existing credit link.

meta.useWhen: The site is small, and the footer only needs to answer where, when and who.
meta.avoidWhen: The site has many pages that visitors look for at the bottom. Use footer-columns.

items.name: footer-columns
items.title: Column footer
items.description: A brand block with description and action beside titled link columns, over a bottom bar for copyright, legal links and a credit.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/FooterColumns.astro. In a Site Boulder site, render it from SiteFooter.astro and pass the existing credit link.

meta.useWhen: The site has enough pages that a footer sitemap genuinely helps visitors.
meta.avoidWhen: There are fewer than six links in total. Use footer-minimal.

items.name: footer-wordmark
items.title: Wordmark footer
items.description: Footer links and a note above the site name set across the full width, sized from its length, with an inverse or plain tone.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/FooterWordmark.astro. Use a short name; tune fit if the face is unusually wide.

meta.useWhen: The name is short and the rest of the site is quiet, so the footer can be the one expressive brand moment.
meta.avoidWhen: The header already shows a large wordmark, or the name runs past about sixteen characters. A repeated giant wordmark reads as filler.

items.name: footer-cta
items.title: Call-to-action footer
items.description: A closing band with one invitation and up to two actions, merged with a compact footer row, in inverse, accent or surface tone.
items.author: Lambda Curry <https://github.com/lambda-curry>
items.docs: Import from src/components/blocks/FooterCta.astro. In a Site Boulder site, render it from SiteFooter.astro and pass the existing credit link.

meta.useWhen: Every page should end by offering the same next step, such as booking or getting in touch.
meta.avoidWhen: The page already ends with a strong call to action, or there is no concrete next step to offer.
